heuristics.name: shared-function-random-mapping
heuristics.statement: One fixed r=64 r-adding walk function with a uniform table and wrapping residues from P uniform starts matches uniform random sampling for exploration statistics (rho length, pooled collision distribution, tail hits, distinguished-key bit uniformity above the distinguished window), and a solved collision is degenerate with probability 1/q.
heuristics.support: Single heuristic bridge (Teske large-r analysis/experiments, record computations, same-regime toys); everything downstream rigorous (van Oorschot-Wiener pooling, birthday inequality, geometric tails, balls-in-bins table occupancy over walk randomness, quantified 1/q degeneracy). No hash function or hash heuristic exists. P-256 field costs bounded analytically (F_p256<=304).

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
Success relies on the supported multi-walk random-mapping heuristic.
Instruction budgets are conservative analytic upper bounds, not measured assembly.
The 2^98-entry table is an analytic device, as is the baseline's larger table.
Beats the generic BSGS control via batched parallel rho at the 0.39 threshold; not novel cryptanalysis.
Supersedes v12: hash-free table, SOS+REDC F_p256<=304 with explicit carries, 6 subs/step, claim 129.02.
